chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who is afflicted by flatulence in his belly while he is able to bear it; should he pray in that state or not pray? He said, 'If he can endure the flatulence and does not fear rushing to pray [due to the fear of the prayer time expiring], let him pray and let him bear it.'
ai.seo_question: Should I continue praying if I have flatulence during the prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *najasat al-batin* (internal impurity) during prayer, emphasizing that minor, manageable emissions do not invalidate the prayer if the worshipper can endure them without haste. It highlights the Shia principle of *al-asl al-sihha* (presumption of validity), where the default state of prayer remains intact unless the disturbance becomes overwhelming or causes significant distraction. This ruling balances ease (*taysir*) with the requirement of *khushu* (focus), ensuring that believers are not burdened by excessive rigor in daily worship.
